meta.title: Deep Time Atlas
meta.canonicalNote: All times are internally normalised to years before 2000 CE. Positive is past. The present is a negative number, which is deliberate: it keeps the origin fixed so the file does not silently change meaning next year.
meta.dataStatusNote: Values in this file are rough figures written from memory to prove the schema. Every record carries a src array that is currently either empty or points at the source that SHOULD supply it. Nothing here has been checked.

confidence.label: Recorded
confidence.note: From written records of variable reliability.

confidence.label: Dated
confidence.note: Radiometric or equivalent, with a stated interval.

confidence.label: Modelled
confidence.note: Output of a model, not an observation.

confidence.label: Inferred
confidence.note: Deduced from sparse or proxy evidence.

confidence.label: Fabricated
confidence.note: Invented for layout. Must not survive to release.

hyde.title: HYDE 3.3 — History Database of the Global Environment
hyde.note: Standard source for gridded population and land use from 10,000 BCE.

westerhold.title: CENOGRID — astronomically dated benthic record
westerhold.note: 66 Myr of climate. The backbone of the deep-time climate lane.

epica.title: EPICA Dome C ice core, 800 kyr

p3k14c.title: p3k14c — global archaeological radiocarbon database
p3k14c.note: About 180,000 dates. The obvious basis for an evidence-density lane that is computed rather than asserted.

seshat.title: Seshat Global History Databank
seshat.note: Rich but methodologically contested. If used, the contestation should be surfaced in the UI, not hidden.

morris.title: The Measure of Civilization
morris.note: Energy capture index. Figures must be re-keyed by hand from published tables.

placeholder.title: No source — placeholder
placeholder.note: Written from memory during pilot construction. Must be replaced.

geo.note: The only lane here with an international standards body behind it.

records.label: Holocene
records.note: One of very few boundaries here fixed by ratified definition rather than estimate: a specific horizon in the NGRIP ice core.

records.label: Anthropocene?
records.note: Proposed as a formal epoch and voted down in 2024. Kept on the chart because the argument is real: proposed start dates have ranged from the Neolithic to the 1960s.

climate.note: This curve is generated from sine waves. It is not data of any kind. It exists to prove the lane renders and must be replaced by CENOGRID + LR04 + EPICA + PAGES 2k, with the splice points between records made visible.

hominins.note: Ranges are first and last appearance dates in a sparse fossil record. Absence of fossils is not absence of the species; the faded ends carry that.

records.label: Sahelanthropus
records.note: One badly distorted skull. Whether it is a hominin at all is argued.

records.label: Au. afarensis
records.note: Lucy's species; among the better-sampled early hominins.

records.label: Au. africanus
records.note: South African cave deposits are notoriously hard to date.

records.label: H. habilis
records.note: Arguably a wastebasket taxon; some material may belong elsewhere.

records.label: H. erectus
records.note: The longest-lived member of our genus by a wide margin.

records.label: H. heidelbergensis
records.note: Increasingly treated as a label of convenience rather than a species.

records.label: H. naledi
records.note: Dated only in 2017. The deposit's interpretation remains actively disputed.

records.label: Denisovans
records.note: Defined largely from DNA plus a handful of fragments. The range is close to a guess.

records.label: H. floresiensis
records.note: Dates were revised drastically in 2016. Expect more revision.

records.label: H. sapiens
records.note: Jebel Irhoud pushed this back. The boundary of 'anatomically modern' is a definition, not an observation.

population.note: Before about 1800 these are reconstructions; before 10 ka they are carrying-capacity models wearing the costume of a census. The band width is the honest part of this lane.

energy.note: Follows the general shape of Ian Morris's energy-capture index. The numbers are invented. This is the lane that makes the fossil-fuel discontinuity visible as something other than a date.

polity.note: A Histomap-style impression of what share of living people fell under which kind of authority. Nobody has these numbers, and the categories are themselves contested — 'chiefdom' in particular is a mid-century construct many anthropologists now reject. The prettier this lane looks, the more it lies.
polity.reviewFlag: Consider cutting or reframing this lane. See NOTES.

regions.note: Regional labels are conveniences of description, not entities that existed. They are also anachronistic before roughly 50 ka and misleading before 2 Ma, which is why this lane does not exist at those scales.

records.label: Neolithic
records.note: Where the fullest early evidence for farming survives — which is not the same as where it first happened.

records.label: Rome
records.note: The end date is a choice, not a fact. 476, 1453, or never, depending on what you think Rome was.

records.label: First settlement
records.note: One of the most actively disputed questions in archaeology. Claims run from about 15 ka to well over 30 ka, and the evidence at each end is contested on methodological grounds.

schemes.note: The point of this lane is disagreement. Switching schemes cuts the same millennia in incompatible ways, and one of them refuses to apply at all.

threeage.label: Three-age system
threeage.note: Devised by Christian Jürgensen Thomsen in 1830s Denmark to sort a museum collection. It was never meant as a universal history and does not work as one.

items.label: Bronze Age
items.note: Begins roughly 900 years later than in Anatolia. Same label, different world, and the label hides that.

items.label: Scheme does not apply
items.note: There is no Bronze Age here, and describing 65,000 years of continuous occupation as 'Stone Age' says more about the classifier than the classified. A periodisation built for Eurasia silently erases everywhere it does not fit.

bighistory.label: Big History thresholds
bighistory.note: David Christian's eight thresholds of rising complexity. Ambitious in scope, and openly teleological — it is a story with a direction built in.

items.label: 5 · Life
items.note: Loosely constrained and keeps moving earlier.

modes.label: Modes of production
modes.note: The Marxian sequence. Its universality was contested from the start, including by Marx, who worried openly about whether it applied outside Western Europe.

climate.label: Climate-led
climate.note: Periodisation by climate state rather than by material culture or politics. Rearranges what counts as a turning point.

items.label: Holocene stability
items.note: The unusually stable interval in which all agriculture, and therefore everything downstream of it, happened.

evidence.note: This lane is not about the past. It is about us: how much we can actually say, era by era. Currently hand-asserted step values. It should be computed — dated archaeological sites per millennium from p3k14c is the obvious candidate, which would make it an observation rather than an opinion.

highlights.label: The Holocene
highlights.note: A formally defined epoch, and one of the few boundaries on this chart with a ratified date attached to a physical layer in an ice core.

highlights.label: Agricultural revolution
highlights.note: Not an event and not one place: at least seven independent centres over several thousand years. The word 'revolution' is doing a great deal of work.

highlights.label: Fossil fuel era
highlights.note: Coal use is far older; sustained fossil-powered growth is roughly 250 years old. At full zoom-out on the linear axis this is thinner than the line drawn to represent it.

highlights.label: Out of Africa
highlights.note: The main dispersal. Earlier excursions are attested but seem to have left little genetic trace. Dates keep moving.

highlights.label: Last Glacial Maximum
highlights.note: Ice at maximum, sea level roughly 120 m lower. The coastlines people actually lived on are now underwater, which biases everything we think we know about this period.

highlights.label: Toba eruption
highlights.note: The eruption is firmly dated. Its supposed bottleneck effect on human populations is disputed and increasingly doubted.

highlights.label: Writing
highlights.note: The sharpest single change in evidence quality anywhere on this chart, and the reason the bottom strip steps up here.
